notes: Two supplied object pronouns ('set it', 'plant it') are added, since neither verb carries an object morpheme (rule 44).

The first chain writes two 'the's: a present article takes the one standing before its own word, so 'the' before 'lofty' goes to the attributive's article and 'the' before 'cedar' to the rectum's, leaving the construct צַמֶּרֶת bare (rules 29, 47).
Each explicit אָנִי takes only its own 'I' while the verb keeps its auxiliary (rules 17, 20).
